subtitle: A Poet, a Pillar, and the Birth of a Written Lineage

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot of Kubja beside a towering stone pillar in a temple courtyard at dusk
panels.action: Kubja of Talagunda stands with stylus in hand beside an uncarved granite pillar near the Praneshvara temple, the sky darkening behind him as if the stone itself waits for his words.

dialogue.text: In Talagunda, a court poet named Kubja was ordered to do the unthinkable — turn royal memory into Sanskrit poetry and carve it forever into stone.

i18n.hi: तलगुंड में दरबारी कवि कुब्ज को हुक्म मिला – राज-स्मृतियों को संस्कृत कविता बनाकर सदा के लिए पत्थर पर उकेरो।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Talagunda village and Praneshvara temple complex nestled by fields and trees
panels.action: A serene view of the Praneshvara temple at Talagunda in the mid-5th century, with villagers, priests and young students moving between shrine, wells and stone platforms.

dialogue.text: Around the mid-5th century, in the quiet settlement of Talagunda, a temple to Praneshvara watched over fields, scholars and scribes as kings rose and fell beyond its trees.

i18n.hi: पाँचवीं सदी के बीचोंबीच, शांत तलगुंड बस्ती में प्रणेश्वर मंदिर खेतों, पंडितों और लेखकों पर नज़र रखता था, जबकि पेड़ों के पार राजा उठते-गिरते रहे।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot inside a simple hall, scrolls and palm-leaves laid out, Kubja seated cross-legged
panels.action: Kubja sits in a small pillared hall, palm-leaf manuscripts beside him, his face lined with concentration as he traces syllables in the dust with his finger.

dialogue.text: Among them lived Kubja, a Sanskrit poet and court scholar, trained to weigh each syllable, each image, until language itself felt like finely hammered metal.

i18n.hi: यहीं रहता था कुब्ज – संस्कृत कवि, दरबारी विद्वान; हर अक्षर, हर छवि को तौलता, जब तक भाषा खुद ठोंके हुए लोहे-सी न चमक उठे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Kubja in a royal audience hall before an unseen seated king, focus on Kubja’s attentive face
panels.action: In a modest but dignified court, Kubja stands with joined palms before the shadowed figure of King Santivarma Kadamba, who sits on a low throne surrounded by counselors.

dialogue.text: His patron was Santivarma of the Kadamba line, a king who ruled from Banavasi yet looked to Talagunda’s shrine and scholars as anchors of his family’s story.

i18n.hi: उसका आश्रयदाता था कदंब वंश का शांतिवर्मा – जो बनावसी से राज करता, पर अपने कुल की कथा के लिए तलगुंड के देव और विद्वानों को सहारा मानता।

panels.shot: close-up on Kubja’s face as he listens, with a faint mix of pride and anxiety
panels.action: Kubja looks up, half-lit by a shaft of light, as Santivarma leans forward, his hand raised in command, though the king’s features remain indistinct.

dialogue.speaker: kubja
dialogue.text: You wish your lineage sung in stone, Maharaja? As polished kavya?

i18n.hi: “आप अपनी वंशावली पत्थर पर गाई हुई चाहते हैं, महाराज? वह भी तराशा हुआ काव्य?”

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot from behind Kubja, showing courtiers gesturing to a rough granite pillar outside
panels.action: Through the open side of the hall, a raw, uncarved pillar stands upright in the temple courtyard, courtiers pointing at it as they speak, with Kubja watching intently.

dialogue.text: Santivarma wanted more than a record of grants and borders. He wanted a crafted poem, thirty and more verses, to bind his house to gods, battles and teachers.

i18n.hi: शांतिवर्मा को केवल दान और सीमाओं का ब्यौरा नहीं चाहिए था। उसे चाहिए था घड़ा हुआ काव्य – तीस से अधिक श्लोक, जो उसके घर को देवताओं, युद्धों और गुरुओं से जोड़े।

panels.shot: low-angle close-up of Kubja’s hand holding a stylus, hovering over a palm-leaf
panels.action: Kubja’s steady hand grips a metal stylus above a palm-leaf, the faint grooves of letters already visible, a small oil lamp casting a warm circle of light.

dialogue.text: In the Deccan, inscriptions had long marked gifts and victories. But Kubja was asked for something rarer: an inscription shaped like court poetry, in careful Sanskrit meters.

i18n.hi: दक्षिणापथ में शिलालेख पहले से ही दान और विजय का बखान करते थे। पर कुब्ज से कुछ दुर्लभ माँगा गया – दरबारी काव्य की लय वाला, छंदबद्ध संस्कृत शिलालेख।

panels.shot: montage-like medium shot showing Kubja reciting to himself, gesturing with fingers as he counts meter
panels.action: Kubja sits upright, eyes half closed, lips moving as he whispers lines, tapping his fingers on his knee in a measured pattern to test the cadence.

dialogue.text: He chose meters that scholars like Kielhorn would one day list: the tight discipline of anuṣṭubh, the sweep of vasanta-tilaka and others, fitting deity, genealogy and war into rhythm.

i18n.hi: उसने वही छंद चुने जिन्हें आगे चलकर कीलहॉर्न जैसे विद्वान गिनेंगे – अनुṣ्टुभ की कसावट, वसंततिलका की फैलावदार चाल, जिनमें देव, वंश और युद्ध सब ताल में बँध जाएँ।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Kubja’s face as he imagines the lineage, faint ghostly silhouettes of ancestors implied behind him
panels.action: Behind Kubja’s focused profile, faint suggestive forms of ancestral figures, teachers and warriors seem to loom, hinting at the dynastic chain he must weave into verse.

dialogue.text: The inscription would tell of Brahmana origins, of a Kadamba ancestor’s insult at Kanchi, of Mayurasharma taking up arms, of kings who followed, of Santivarma himself at the end.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख ब्राह्मण मूल की कथा सुनाता – कांची में कदंब पूर्वज पर हुए अपमान की, मयूरशर्मा के शस्त्र उठाने की, अगली पीढ़ियों की, और अंत में स्वयं शांतिवर्मा की।

panels.shot: medium shot of Kubja presenting a palm-leaf manuscript to a temple priest or court official in the temple courtyard
panels.action: Standing near the base of the pillar, Kubja respectfully offers a bundle of palm-leaves to an older official, with stone-cutters and scribes waiting nearby with tools.

dialogue.text: The poet’s task was only half the work. His verses had to move from leaf and tongue to the stubborn grain of granite, letter by letter, without losing their form.

i18n.hi: कवि का आधा काम तो बस रचना था। बाकी था पत्ती और ज़बान से इन श्लोकों को हट्टीले ग्रेनाइट पर उतारना – अक्षर दर अक्षर – बिना छंद तोड़े।

panels.shot: high-angle shot over the shoulder of a stonecutter as he incises the first letters, Kubja supervising
panels.action: A stonecutter kneels by the pillar, chisel poised, while Kubja stands close, pointing gently at a traced guideline of early Kadamba letters ready to be carved.

dialogue.text: The script followed the Kadamba stream: rounded, early forms that would one day give rise to later Kannada and related southern scripts, yet here they carried Sanskrit sounds.

i18n.hi: लिपि कदंब धारा की थी – गोल, शुरुआती रूप, जो आगे चलकर कन्नड़ और दक्षिणी लिपियों में ढलने वाले थे, पर यहाँ वही संस्कृत ध्वनियाँ ढो रहे थे।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of a line of freshly cut Kadamba letters on the pillar, stone dust still clinging
panels.action: A line of crisp, newly carved characters marches across the pillar’s face, tiny curls of stone dust still clinging to the grooves, catching the sun.

dialogue.text: Each carved syllable bore two memories at once: the polished sound of court Sanskrit, and the visual discipline of a regional script line still finding its own shapes.

i18n.hi: हर खुदा हुआ अक्षर दो यादें ढोता था – दरबारी संस्कृत की तराशी हुई ध्वनि, और आकार खोजती एक नई, अनुशासित प्रादेशिक लिपि।

panels.shot: medium shot of Kubja and craftsmen working together, pillar partially covered in inscription
panels.action: The pillar now carries several completed lines; Kubja, the stonecutter and a scribe huddle at its base, cross-checking the palm-leaf as more space is measured out above.

dialogue.speaker: kubja
dialogue.text: Do not crowd the meter. The verse must still breathe on stone.

i18n.hi: “छंद मत घुटाओ, श्लोक को पत्थर पर भी साँस लेनी है।”

panels.shot: wide shot of the nearly finished pillar standing tall near the Praneshvara temple, villagers watching
panels.action: The nearly fully inscribed pillar stands upright, its dense lines gleaming faintly, as villagers and students gather at a respectful distance, whispering among themselves.

dialogue.text: By the time Kubja’s poem reached its final verses, the pillar had become more than stone. It was now a vertical manuscript, raised under open sky, addressed to gods, men and time.

i18n.hi: जब तक कुब्ज की कविता अंतिम पंक्तियों तक पहुँची, स्तंभ सिर्फ पत्थर न रहा – वह खुली हवा में खड़ा ऊर्ध्व पांडुलिपि बन गया, देवों, मनुष्यों और काल से मुखातिब।

panels.shot: close-up on Kubja’s face as he reads aloud from the stone, eyes tracing the letters
panels.action: Kubja stands close to the pillar, fingertips lightly touching the carved lines as he recites, his eyes moving steadily from character to character.

dialogue.text: The inscription itself would one day state that Kubja composed this kavya and had it placed on stone by Santivarma’s order, tying author, patron and object in a single claim.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख खुद एक दिन बताएगा कि यह काव्य कुब्ज ने रचा और शांतिवर्मा के आदेश से पत्थर पर बसाया – लेखक, आश्रयदाता और वस्तु को एक ही दावे में बाँधते हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Santivarma and Kubja before the pillar, king’s hand resting on the stone
panels.action: Santivarma stands beside the pillar, his hand resting on its inscribed surface, while Kubja bows slightly nearby, the temple entrance in the background.

dialogue.text: For Santivarma, the pillar was a public answer to doubt: here was a clear genealogy, a shaped past, a declaration that the Kadambas stood not by accident but by cosmic and learned design.

i18n.hi: शांतिवर्मा के लिए यह स्तंभ संदेह का सार्वजनिक जवाब था – यहाँ थी साफ वंशावली, गढ़ा हुआ अतीत, ऐलान कि कदंब संयोग नहीं, नियति और विद्या से खड़े हैं।

panels.shot: soft-focus shot of the pillar weathering over time, subtle changes in surroundings suggesting centuries passing
panels.action: The same pillar stands as seasons blur around it: rains darkening the stone, creepers growing and receding, the temple structures shifting as time passes.

dialogue.text: Centuries would pass. Dynasties around Banavasi would rise, fracture and vanish, but Kubja’s verses, now mute lines of stone, stayed in the village wind.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ बीत गईं। बनावसी के आसपास राजघराने उठे, बिखरे, मिट गए, पर कुब्ज के श्लोक, अब पत्थर की मौन पंक्तियाँ, गाँव की हवा में बने रहे।

panels.shot: modern-era scholar in the foreground copying the inscription, pillar behind; Kubja’s faint spectral figure suggested beside the pillar
panels.action: A colonial-era scholar in simple European attire bends over a notebook, copying the pillar’s lines, while a faint, almost transparent hint of Kubja’s figure stands beside the stone.

dialogue.text: In the 19th and 20th centuries, editors like Rice, Kielhorn and Sircar would lean close to these letters, teasing out meters, names and dates, hearing Kubja’s craft through their own training.

i18n.hi: उन्नीसवीं–बीसवीं सदी में राइस, कीलहॉर्न और सिर्कार जैसे संपादक इन अक्षरों के करीब झुके – छंद, नाम, तिथियाँ खंगालते, अपने प्रशिक्षण से कुब्ज की कारीगरी सुनते रहे।

panels.shot: interior shot of a modern archaeologist documenting the 2013 Talagunda balustrade find, pillar visible outside through a doorway
panels.action: Inside a modern dig shelter near Talagunda, an archaeologist records a newly uncovered balustrade fragment, while, through the doorway, the old inscription pillar stands in the sunlight.

dialogue.text: New finds at Talagunda, like the 2013 balustrade, would add further layers to the site’s language history, but Kubja’s pillar remained the clearest, self-conscious poem of power there.

i18n.hi: तलगुंड की नई खोजें, जैसे २०१३ की रेलिंग, स्थल की भाषिक परतें बढ़ाती रहीं, पर शक्ति से भरा, स्वयं-सचेत सबसे स्पष्ट काव्य वही पुराना स्तंभ रहा।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of the pillar today, tourists and students looking up, sky bright above
panels.action: The Talagunda pillar stands in the present day, modest yet dignified, as students and visitors look up at its inscribed face, some tracing the ancient letters with their gaze.

dialogue.text: Today we read it as history: a source for Mayurasharma and the Kadambas. Yet it is also an early Deccan example of something quieter — history cast deliberately as artful kavya.

i18n.hi: आज हम इसे इतिहास की तरह पढ़ते हैं – मयूरशर्मा और कदंबों का स्रोत मानकर। पर यह दक्खिन में एक और चीज़ भी है – इतिहास को जान-बूझकर कलात्मक काव्य की शक्ल देने की शुरुआती मिसाल।

panels.shot: final contemplative medium shot of Kubja’s imagined figure seated beneath the pillar, stylus resting on his knee, looking outward
panels.action: An imagined Kubja sits beneath the inscribed pillar at twilight, stylus resting on his knee, as if listening to distant voices of readers yet to come.

dialogue.text: Kubja’s work reminds us that power lasts longer when it learns a form, and that in the meeting of meter, script and stone, memory gains a body that can outlive its makers.

i18n.hi: कुब्ज का काम याद दिलाता है – सत्ता तब तक टिकती है जब तक वह रूप सीख ले; और जब छंद, लिपि और पत्थर मिलते हैं, तब स्मृति को ऐसा शरीर मिलता है जो रचयिताओं से अधिक जीता है।

title_i18n.en: Kubja Carves a Poem in Stone
title_i18n.hi: कुब्ज ने पत्थर पर कविता उकेरी
